0.35 tier: unremedied universal exposure or state-tolerated targeting with inadequate remedy. Here: state forces violence, militia with impunity, Article 176 prosecutions (frequency unknown). Hmm.

But the evidence on the police violence is a travel guide's report, undated-ish, no counts. And there's no trans-specific evidence at all — dossier is generic LGBTQ. Thin data on trans specifics; extrapolate from state violence and impunity.

Compare 0.25 anchors: "In the republic of Talvera, trans presentation not explicitly criminalised, but police repeatedly raid cafés and hotels to detain people..." — documented pattern of raids. Here we don't have documented repeat pattern against trans people specifically; we have generic reports of police violence and torture against LGBTQ people, plus a partial collapse of state authority.

0.35 anchors: Orenna — police routinely stop visibly trans people, photograph passports, extortion; documented repeated stops of foreign travellers. Here less specific.

Also 0.15 anchors: militia controlling transport corridors targeting travellers (Miravel) — that's structurally similar to "armed militia groups in the east committing extreme violence against LGBTQ people with near-total impunity" plus police withdrawal. Hmm, that Miravel anchor is at 0.15. But here militia is confined to the east of the country, and state forces violence elsewhere; the dossier doesn't say militia stops travellers at corridors — it says extreme violence against LGBTQ people. That's severe but geographically partial, and no counts.

Also the impunity: courts don't function to protect — rule of law weak. Under rule 11 liability clause: no working recourse. State is perpetrator.

I'd place this in the 0.20–0.30 range. Weighing: no trans-specific law, but morality provisions applied to LGBTQ with imprisonment possible; state forces commit violence/torture against LGBTQ; militia extreme violence in east with impunity; no remedy; expression censored. That's a documented pattern of state-tolerated/directed harm with no recourse — worse than 0.35 (which involves unremedied facility rules without state violence at scale) and comparable to the 0.25 anchors.

But the evidence is thin/generic (no counts, no trans-specific incidents, travel-guide sourcing). Rule 13/18: undated, unsourced prevalence words are not evidence. But the 2024 stakeholder submission documents the non-protection and Article 176. The travel guide documents police/army violence and militia violence. Also state collapse in parts.

I'll settle around 0.25. Considering travel-guide-level claims with no counts and generic LGBTQ framing (trans-specific exposure less documented), maybe 0.27. And there's a partial-collapse-of-state element raising severity in the east. Also no criminalisation of same-sex conduct at all, and no presentation offence — a mitigating factor relative to 0.15/0.20 cases.
